Team — first-pass sizing below (attached workbook + KV heatmap). Notes and assumptions are inline.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Baseline pool: 8 x NVIDIA H100 80GB (reserved) configured for mixed-precision serving and Q4_0 quantization for the 33B fallback.
- Peak burst capacity: scale to 12 x H100s (burst on-demand) to cover 28 QPS with headroom for 5% 128k requests.
- For latency-sensitive paths and the 70B high-quality model, keep FP16 (or Q6/Q8) to avoid quality regressions; estimate ~2.2x memory reduction at Q6 vs FP16, Q4_0 yields ~3.5x memory reduction but with possible latency/quality variability on long-context prompts.

Sizing detail (per active GPU):
- Model weights (Llama-2-70B, sharded): FP16 working set ~38GB; with Q6 that's ~17GB; with Q4_0 ~11GB (approx).
- KV cache per 1k context tokens: ~0.9GB for the 70B in our runtime (attention keys+values stored per token, depends on kv-compression).
- Working/activation overhead: ~6–8GB per request per GPU for 70B at high concurrency.

Context-driven capacity math (worst-case example):
- 28 QPS with mixed request sizes; assume at peak 10 concurrent long-context 128k sessions (5% of burst):
  - KV footprint for 128k session on 70B: 128 * 0.9GB = ~115GB — which we MUST offload or serve on multi-GPU sharded nodes.
  - Practical approach: route 128k sessions to specialized multi-GPU partitions (4 H100s) with KV offload enabled (NVMe-backed KV shards).

Recommended architecture choices:
1) Two pools:
   - General-purpose pool (8 x H100 reserved): handles 32k/64k calls with Q6 for 70B, Q4_0 for 33B fallback.
   - Long-context partition (4 x H100 on-demand/burst): pinned for 128k sessions with KV offload and larger NVMe cache.
2) Autoscaling: maintain minimum reserved capacity at 8 GPUs; automatic scale adds up to 8 additional GPUs across pools (limit by burst). Use real-time KV-occupancy triggers: when aggregate KV > 60% of pooled NVMe capacity, reject new 128k sessions or fallback to cheaper 33B with contextual slicing.
3) Quantization policy: default to Q6 for 70B in production (best latency-quality tradeoff), Q4_0 on 33B as low-cost fallback. Keep FP16 image for canary/QA to monitor quality drift.

Ops runbook highlight (for procurement):
- Failover: if Dedicated pool under pressure, fallback route: 70B -> 33B Q4 fallback -> queue with token-limited response (notify client via 429).
- Monitoring: per-route KV occupancy, per-GPU memory headroom, p95 latency alarms.
- Escalation: auto-create incident and page on p95 > 4s for >5 minutes.

Costs: rough committed pool estimate (monthly) attached in MAL-quote-v1.pdf; workbook contains per-hour GPU unit math.

Attachments: context-sizing-workbook.xlsx (calc), kv-cache-heatmap.png (visual), MAL-quote-v1.pdf (commercial).
